name: Pedro Sánchez
role: Prime Minister of Spain (2018–present); PSOE leader
summary: Social-democratic prime minister of Spain, leading PSOE-based coalition governments. He combines a strong welfare state, higher minimum wages and taxes on the wealthy with pro-EU and multilateralist foreign policy, feminist and LGTBI rights, and strict regulation of tech platforms. He rejects Catalan secession but granted pardons and an amnesty to its leaders.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Pledged in the 2023 investiture speech to restore universal public healthcare and sharply cut waiting lists.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Promised in 2020 to raise the minimum wage to more decent levels and in 2023 that it would keep rising every year; credits government increases in 2025.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said in 2023 that the rich must pay more in tax and backed levies on big fortunes, banks and energy firms; in 2020 asked the better-off for 'un poquito más'.

unions-good.rationale: Defends social dialogue between unions and employers and criticises PP and Vox for trying to end it; no direct statement on unions generally.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Calls for strict legal regulation, scrutiny and accountability of tech platforms and proposes a 15% minimum effective corporate tax; tight regulation of other sectors is not stated.

cut-welfare.rationale: Pledged to strengthen the welfare state and dependency system and said Spain refused to sacrifice its welfare state to the 5% defence target.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Proposed making platform executives legally liable for failing to remove illegal or hateful content and a 'hate and polarisation footprint'; frames accountability as compatible with free expression.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Has called for abolishing prostitution and said in December 2025 it will pass in future although he lacks a majority now.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cited same-sex marriage with divorce and abortion as rights nobody was forced to use, and promised a state pact for LGTBI people.

abortion-legal.rationale: Defends the right to voluntary termination and in 2026 presented a constitutional reform to shield it.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Rejects treating migrants as enemies, backs integration and ordered an extraordinary regularisation of about 500,000 undocumented migrants; levels as such not addressed.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Wants a stronger UN system with more resources, a reformed Security Council and a stronger International Criminal Court.

free-trade.rationale: Backs the EU-Mercosur deal and says trade wars have no winners, but also wants the EU-China trade relationship rebalanced.

nation-first.rationale: Says abandoning multilateralism would be a historic mistake and defends cooperation through the UN and EU.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate a question of survival, not ideology, and decarbonisation unstoppable; backs the European Green Deal.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Government kept a phase-out calendar by 2035 and Wikipedia describes him as opposing nuclear power, but in 2026 it extended Almaraz to 2030.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Said in a trade war there are never winners; no stated support for protecting domestic industry from competition.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: In 2020 reaffirmed commitment to the parliamentary monarchy as part of the constitutional pact while noting the PSOE once defended a republic.

democracy-best.rationale: Calls democracy the necessary condition of freedom and says electoral results must be respected even if one dislikes them.

right-to-secede.rationale: Rejects Catalan independence, says a united Spain is better, and ruled out a self-determination referendum.

national-self-determination.rationale: Recognised Palestine as a state but rejected independence for Catalonia.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Criticised the PP for removing health cards from migrants and ordered regularisation of undocumented migrants.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Pursues real and effective equality of men and women and a parity law; no distinct legal roles.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Aims for more than half of energy from renewables and calls decarbonisation unstoppable.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Programme is an expanded welfare state, public health and education, and public housing building.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Promised in 2020 freedom of expression and association 'without gag laws, without outlawing political parties'.

party-controls-media.rationale: Said it is not the government's mission to hand out reliability cards to media; his plan stresses independence and pluralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Backs a federal EU, a much larger European budget, and jointly financed European defence and security.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Wants to build public homes for affordable rent, boost rent aid, and protect small landlords.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Doubled Spain's development cooperation budget and raised multilateral contributions.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Pledged support for Ukraine until the last Russian soldier leaves and opposes wars of aggression.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Argues the wealthy should pay more income tax.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Says democracy exists only within the Constitution and accuses the right of muzzling the judiciary.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Promised a parity law to break glass ceilings.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: In 2026 proposed a constitutional reform to shield abortion from future majorities and a constitutional change on dignity in article 49.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Ordered Franco's exhumation from the Valley of the Fallen and criticised the restoration of Francoist street names.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pensions to stay in the public system revalued with inflation by law.

corporate-influence.rationale: Brought a lobbying regulation bill and speaks of powerful economic elites; no explicit statement on campaign money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Said the government wants to encourage births and announced a family law; incentives not specified and migration also backed.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Announced a National Open Government Strategy and an Open Administration Law to expand government information.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Contrasts regional governments that privatise hospitals with his own funding of public services.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Promised a state pact for LGTBI people and defends LGTBI rights.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Promised broader freedom of expression and association and said opposing parties should not be outlawed.

assisted-dying.rationale: His government challenged Madrid's veto of the euthanasia law and defended the law.

social-market-economy.rationale: Combines a market economy with a strong welfare state, social dialogue and labour protection.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Keeps Spain's armed forces and troops in 16 countries across missions, at about 2.1% GDP defence spending.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Describes tech billionaires with near-total economic power as seeking to undermine democracy.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Contrasts others' privatisation with government providing resources to public services.

rent-control.rationale: Government designated 304 stressed housing zones under the housing law and wants to curb speculation.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Describes Gaza as genocide and condemned it at the UN.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Opposes hospital privatisation and gives resources to public services.

online-anonymity.rationale: Wants to end anonymity on social networks, with one real identity document per user and only registry-linked pseudonyms.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Says Spain opposed all wars of aggression, though also takes part in international missions.

arms-reduction.rationale: Called at the UN for rebuilding nuclear non-proliferation and disarmament frameworks and refused 5% GDP defence spending.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Credits a labour reform negotiated with social partners and backs social dialogue.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Urged strengthening the ICC so violators answer, and proposed an ICJ opinion on Israel's obligations.

notes: Sources are mainly his own speeches on lamoncloa.gob.es. Spain recognised Palestine in 2024 and imposed an arms embargo on Israel in 2025. The Almaraz nuclear extension in 2026 makes his nuclear position mixed. The amnesty, Western Sahara shift, trans law and Mercosur support were found in news only, so are not answered or are low.
